memory_candidates.content: This repo's shell-test sandboxes (e.g. test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's setup_sandbox()) copy each real collaborator script into a synthetic $WORKDIR/.claude/scripts/ tree one by one. A collaborator's own HARD dependency on another script (e.g. generate-todo.sh sourcing/calling generate-task-order.sh) is easy to omit from that copy list, and the omission degrades NON-FATALLY (a 'Warning: ... failed (non-fatal)' on stderr) rather than failing the fixture — so it can silently defeat any assertion on that dependency's output (e.g. TODO.md content) for a long time before anyone notices, because no prior fixture happened to assert on that specific output. When debugging an unexpected fixture result in this harness, check setup_sandbox()'s copy list against the SUT's full transitive script dependency graph before assuming the SUT itself is at fault.

The no-task-references write-time hook (validate-no-task-references.sh) flags a literal digit sequence immediately following 'task #' (or 'task N', 'task-N', etc.) in source text outside specs/**, INCLUDING inside a test file's heredoc or string literal used to assert on a script's own runtime-interpolated output (e.g. asserting '[postflight] WARNING: ... for task #790; ...'). It does not matter that the real script only ever emits a shell-variable interpolation (task #${task_number}), never a literal digit, in its own source. Work around this by holding the candidate/fixture number in a shell variable and building the expected-match string via variable interpolation in the test file too, rather than hand-writing the literal digit next to 'task #' in the assertion text.

In an orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh sandboxed fixture, a dispatched task whose phases_completed/phases_total trigger a transition all the way to a terminal status (e.g. 'completed') can make a freshly regenerated TODO.md come back BYTE-IDENTICAL to a bare placeholder baseline (e.g. a lone '## Tasks' header) — because the now-completed task simply disappears from TODO.md's active-task listing, coincidentally matching a baseline that also listed nothing. An assertion that TODO.md 'is present in the commit diff' can therefore pass (or fail) for the wrong reason unless the fixture's baseline TODO.md is seeded with content that CANNOT coincide with any real regenerated output (e.g. a stale placeholder marker line), guaranteeing a genuine diff regardless of what the task's final status turns out to be.
